##### Legal gender recognition

###### UN MEMBER STATES

 - LGR Based on Self-ID

AT LEAST- Where surgery or sterilisation is required

AT LEAST- Where a diagnosis is required

##### About this section

This section tracks laws and regulations that provide for legal procedures to amend a person’s name and gender marker in identity documents. These two procedures grant trans and gender diverse people the ability to hold IDs that match their identity and expression, which in turn assists them to access other rights and services in their everyday lives.

Name change processes are especially relevant for countries where gender marker change is not possible or is otherwise onerous, medicalised, pathologised and, therefore, restrictive.

The chart for gender marker change disaggregates the requirements imposed by local legal frameworks on people who wish to have their gender markers amended, including gender affirming surgery, forced sterilisation, diagnosis, hormone treatment, real life test, expert testimony, witnesses, forced divorce or having no children.

Additionally, information is provided where jurisdictions provide for gender marker change for children and the possibility of opting for a non-binary gender marker.

- Kyrgyzstan

Parliament passed in the first reading a bill that would ban legal gender recognition. June 2026
- Mexico

Queretaro's legislature passed a decree establishing a procedure based on self-ID to change someone's gender markers. April 2026
- Costa Rica

A new bill allowing people to decide whether their ID cards would show their legal gender has been introduced. April 2026
- India

Parliament approved a bill explicitly removing self-ID from the Transgender Rights Act 2019, narrowing the definition of transgender and imposing pathologising requirements for legal gender recognition. March 2026
- Bulgaria

The Court of Justice of the European Union ruled in a case involving Bulgaria that the refusal of an EU Member State to recognise the change of name and gender legally acquired by an EU citizen in a different EU Member state is contrary to EU Law. March 2026
- Ecuador

The Constitutional Court ruled that the requirement to be 18 years old in order to access legal gender recognition was unconstitutional. March 2026
- Portugal

Two bills banning legal gender recognition for children and re-introducing pathologising requirements for adults have been introduced. March 2026
- Mexico

The Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation ruled that the requirement in Guerrero's legislation to be 18 years old in order to access legal gender recognition in was unconstitutional. March 2026
- Austria

The Constitutional Court has extended the right to legal gender recognition to non binary people. December 2025
- Mexico

The Supreme Court has struck down a provision from Campeche's legislation that only allowed adults to access legal gende recognition. December 2025
- Slovakia

The Constitution has been amended to ban legal gender recognition. November 2025
- US Virgin Islands (USA)

The Governor issued an executive order creating a procedure to change someone's legal gender. October 2025
- Kenya

The High Court issued an interim order to amend the birth certificate of an intersex man to reflect their gender identity. September 2025
- Kenya

The High Court has ruled that the government must legally recognise trans people's gender identity and safeguard their constitutional rights. August 2025
- Cuba

The new Civil Registry Law has eased the requirements for legal gender recognition, although it still falls short from self-ID. July 2025
- Puerto Rico (USA)

The Federal Court in San Juan has ordered the government of Puerto Rico to include an “X” marker on applications to change the gender stated on birth certificates. May 2025
- Mexico

In December 2024, the Guanajauto Congress approved a simplified procedure for legal gender recognition based solely on self-perception. December 2024
- Greece

A far-right party introduced a bill to ban legal gender recognition and gender affirming care for children. November 2024
- Argentina

An MP introduced a bill aimed at banning legal gender recognition for children and people who had been convicted of any crime. November 2024
- Romania

The Court of Justice of the European Union ruled in a case involving Romania that the refusal of a EU Member State to recognise the change of name and gender legally acquired by a EU citizen in a different EU Member state is contrary to EU Law. October 2024
- Georgia

The Bill on Family Values and Protection of Minors, which bans legal gender recognition, has been adopted by Parliament after the President refused to sign it into law. October 2024
- Georgia

The Bill on Family Values and Protection of Minors, which bans legal gender recognition and punishes gender-affirming care, was adopted in its third reading. September 2024
- Nepal

The Supreme Court declared the right of a trans woman to be legally recognised as a woman in her documents for the first time. July 2024
- Japan

A bill has been introduced to remove the legal requirements of undergoing an sterilization surgery and having no minor children. June 2024
- Mexico

The Congress of Baja California adopted Bill No. 43 (2024), which allows legal gender recognition for children in the state. June 2024
- Spain

The Government of Spain challenged Community of Madrid's Law No. 17 (2023) before the Constitutional Court, suspending its effects. June 2024
- Malta

New law allowing for the legal recognition of people with a non-binary gender identity and reducing the age to apply for legal gender recognition to 16 has been passed. June 2024
- Mexico

Yucatan passed the Civil Registry Law Amendment Bill (2023) establishing an administrative process for legally recognising gender identity based solely on self-identification. April 2024
- Montenegro

The Draft Law on Legal Recognition of Gender Identity Based on Self-Determination (2024) was introduced, proposing gender marker changes without invasive requirements. March 2024
- Japan

The Okayama Family Court recognised a transgender man's petition to legally change his gender without undergoing sterilisation surgery. February 2024
- Ecuador

The National Assembly approved an amendment to the Organic Law on Civil Identity and Data Management (2024) which allows anyone over 18 years old to change their "sex" or "gender" markers based on self-ID. January 2024
- Vietnam

The Drafting Committee for the Law on Gender Change organised a consultation seminar with experts who recommended that legal aid must be mandatory throughout the process and that this service should be provided without any associated costs. January 2024
- United States of America

In Iowa, a federal judge preliminarily blocked the enforcement of HB 71 in Poe v. Labrador (2023). December 2023
- United Kingdom

The Department of Education released a draft of Non-statutory transgender guidance for schools and colleges (2023). Trans children would only be permitted to change their name if it were deemed in "the best interests of the child" and parents have been fully consulted. December 2023
- Vietnam

The Committee for the Draft Law on Gender Change (2023) released the bill for public input, holding consultations with the transgender community. The bill outlines legal gender recognition processes, including required medical interventions. December 2023
- Spain

Law No. 17 (2023) was enacted in the Community of Madrid. The law is considered to be the first regression in the rights of LGBT people in Spain. December 2023
- Japan

After the Superme Court ruling, the Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare, along with the Ministry of Justice, officially ended the requirement for doctor's certificates to determine reproductive capacity in legal gender recognition applications. December 2023
- United Kingdom

The Court of Session, as part of Scotland’s highest court, ruled that the UK government had acted lawfully in blocking the enactment of the Scottish government’s Gender Recognition Reform (Scotland) Bill. December 2023
- Ecuador

The Law to modify the Organic Law for the Management of Identity and Civil Data (2022) was passed. The law amends Article 94 to insert a procedure to rectify registry data related to "sex" based on Self-ID. December 2023
- Slovakia

The newly issued Public Health Standard (2023), which eliminated the forced sterilisation requirement for changing the gender marker, was revoked by the new Health Minister, raising concerns about the potential reinstatement of the forced sterilisation requirement. November 2023
- Chile

A Family Court of Santiago set a precedent by recognising the right of a 10-year-old trans girl to rectify her name and sex under the Law that Recognises and Protects the Right to Gender Identity (2018). November 2023
- South Korea

The National Assembly announced the Legal Gender Recognition Bill (2023), which would remove mandatory medical treatment for applicants, including gender-affirming surgery. November 2023
- Pakistan

The Sindh Human Rights Commission (SHRC) demanded that the National Database Registration Authority (Nadra) issue identity cards to transgender persons without any discrimination. October 2023
- Japan

The Supreme Court unanimously declared mandatory sterilisation for legal gender recognition unconstitutional, citing it as a breach of individual freedom and invasive procedures. October 2023
- Italy

Italian courts allowed gender marker changes without surgery in two landmark cases, building upon a 2015 Court of Cassation ruling. October 2023
- Puerto Rico (USA)

House Bill 1,889 (2023) was introduced to ban gender-affirmative procedures for individuals under 21 years old, including hormone treatments and surgeries. October 2023
- Iceland

Bill No. 103 (2023) was introduced to provide for dual passports to individuals identified as "gender neutral" in the national registry. September 2023
- Thailand

MP Padi Pat Santipada received a petition including a draft Royal Decree for self-identified legal gender recognition. September 2023
- Paraguay

An Appellate Court reversed a First Instance Court's decision to allow a transgender name change. September 2023
- Taiwan (China)

The Supreme Administrative Court ruled that the Household Registration Act (2015) does not require surgery as a mandatory criterion to change one's legal gender. September 2023
- Australia

In New South Wales, a bill was introduced to allow people over the age of 16 to change their gender markers on identifying documents without surgery. August 2023
- Colombia

The Foreign Affairs Ministry announced that it would include the "X" category in the gender field in the Colombian passport. August 2023
- Pakistan

After the Federal Shariat Court’s regressive decision, the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) suspended the registration of transgender individuals, specifically the issuance of ID cards bearing an "X" gender marker. July 2023
- Russia

President Vladimir Putin signed into law a ban on any form of legal gender recognition and any intervention aimed at changing the sex of a person. July 2023
- Iraq

A bill was submitted to punish "acts of effeminacy" with imprisonment for one to three years or a fine. It also forbids changing a person's "biological sex based on psychological desires", with similar penalties, except for treating "congenital anomalies". July 2023
- Brazil

The Ministry of Social Security issued Ordinance No. 1,945 (2023). Under Article 2 of the ordinance "transsexuals and travestis" are afforded the right to choose their nominal treatment in acts and procedures wit
